title: Canonical derived scalar Hom equivalence
statement: The derived scalar extension and exact restriction admit an equivalence of Hom sets whose value on a morphism f is adicReductionDerivedUnit ≫ Res.map f.

proof.text: Apply derivedChangeOfRingsGeneral to the constant quotient coefficient map. Use the proved generic tensorAdjunction_of_identifications helper of DerivedScalarExtensionRestrictionAdjunction: the change-of-rings functor is left adjoint to exact restriction, with unit m ↦ 1 tensor m. Resolve every homotopy object by exists_isKFlatResolutionGeneral. Its K-flat counit is invertible, so the proved generic derivedAdjunction_of_resolutions helper supplies the derived adjunction and its unit compatibility.

source.place: Proof step 6, derivation of the scalar adjunction

proof.text: Identify the termwise extension functor on the chosen K-flat complex with adicChange by its recorded object and morphism equalities. Transport the derived Hom equivalence along the K-flat counit, quotientCompQhIso, this termwise identification, and the chosen realization. The ordinary complex unit followed by the identification agrees with adicReductionAugmentation: both send every local section m to 1 tensor m, and the augmentation uniqueness theorem applies. Naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors and its homotopy factorization then identifies the transported unit with adicReductionDerivedUnit. Postcomposition by restriction of f gives the required formula.

proof.text: Define the reduction of an arbitrary derived morphism by the inverse canonical Hom equivalence applied to postcomposition with the target unit. Injectivity proves the unit square, identity and composition laws, and reduction preserves isomorphisms by reducing an inverse.
